Remedy Robotics Raises $62 Million Series B to Bring Life-Saving Cardiovascular Intervention to Patients Everywhere
News provided by
Remedy Robotics, Inc.
Nov 16, 2026, 10:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Funding will support clinical trials, advancement toward FDA approval, and planned commercial deployment of the company's AI-enabled endovascular robotic platform and software suite
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Remedy Robotics, Inc. ("Remedy"), a leading healthcare and physical AI company developing robotic systems for cardiovascular care and endovascular intervention, today announced it has raised $62 million in Series B funding to accelerate its mission of delivering flawless, immediate robotic care to all patients, regardless of location.
The funding will support several major milestones, including a planned pivotal clinical trial in partnership with the University of California and advancement toward FDA approval for neurovascular intervention. Remedy will also deploy prototype N1 Systems across its network of clinical partners, including through its strategic partnerships with SVIN Mission Thrombectomy and the Australian Stroke Alliance, while continuing to advance the system's industry-leading AI capabilities and autonomous functions.
"Endovascular intervention is the gold standard treatment for stroke and many cardiovascular emergencies, yet access remains limited to a small number of hospitals. For these time-critical conditions, that's devastating. Even when specialist intervention is available, treatment is often delayed, and complications are frustratingly common," said Dr. David Bell, CEO and Co-founder of Remedy Robotics . "This funding will allow us to accelerate toward deployment of our N1 System so we can bring quality intervention to patients everywhere, regardless of geography."
DCVC led the Series B, with participation from new investors including UC Investments (the University of California's investment office), Skip Capital, and Hostplus (one of Australia's largest pension funds). Existing investors Build Collective by Tony Fadell, Blackbird, Divergent Capital and KdT Ventures doubled down.
"Remedy Robotics represents a new generation of medical robotics and physical AI companies, focused not only on technical innovation, but on solving real-world challenges," said James Hardiman, General Partner at DCVC . "We believe the company is uniquely positioned to redefine how life-saving intervention is delivered and are thrilled to support them as they advance toward broader clinical and commercial adoption."
Remedy is finalizing development of the N1 System, an AI-enabled robotic platform and software suite that uses machine learning to analyze preoperative imaging, simulate cases in advance, provide real-time 3D-2D image registration and complete entire endovascular procedures robotically. Designed for on-site, remote, or autonomous operation, the system has the potential to dramatically expand access to and improve the quality of specialized neurovascular, coronary, and peripheral vascular care. Remedy now works with more than 100 hospitals worldwide and is among a small group of physical AI companies bringing robotics into real-world clinical use. In October 2025, Remedy announced that it had successfully completed the world's first remote neurointerventional procedures using the N1 System.

Oyster Therapeutics: $60 Million Series A-2 Funding To Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Development And Protein Degradation Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:19 AM
Oyster Therapeutics: $60 Million Series A-2 Funding To Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Development And Protein Degradation Platform
Oyster Therapeutics, formerly known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, has raised $60 million in Series A-2 funding to advance its next-generation targeted protein degradation technology for Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. The financing will support the development of the company’s lead oral tau degrader toward clinical trials while expanding its proprietary SELFTAC drug discovery platform. The round was led by 4BIO Capital, a London-based venture capital firm specializing in life sciences, with participation from new investors Eli Lilly and Company, CE Ventures, Actium Group, and TOHO Ventures, which is managed by Global Brain.
Existing investors Syncona, Oxford Science Enterprises, Mission BioCapital, and MGB Ventures also participated.
The financing comes as the company rebrands from Kesmalea Therapeutics to Oyster Therapeutics, reflecting its transition toward clinical development and broader ambitions in neuroscience.
Headquartered in London, Oyster is developing medicines based on targeted protein degradation, a therapeutic approach designed to eliminate disease-associated proteins by using the body’s natural cellular protein disposal mechanisms.
Unlike conventional treatments that may inhibit the activity of particular proteins, targeted protein degraders are designed to trigger their removal from cells.
Oyster is initially focusing on neurodegenerative diseases involving abnormal accumulations of the tau protein.
Tau plays an important role in maintaining healthy neuronal structures, but abnormal forms can accumulate and contribute to diseases known as tauopathies.
Alzheimer’s disease is among the best-known conditions associated with pathological tau accumulation.
The company’s lead program is an orally administered, brain-penetrant tau degrader designed to selectively remove harmful forms of tau while preserving healthy tau.
Developing medicines capable of reaching the central nervous system presents considerable challenges because the blood-brain barrier restricts the passage of many therapeutic compounds.
Traditional bifunctional protein degraders can be relatively large molecules, limiting their ability to cross biological membranes and reach brain tissue.
Oyster’s proprietary SELFTAC platform is designed to address this limitation by enabling larger targeted protein degraders to function as smaller molecular components.
The technology uses a reversible linker connecting two molecular structures, commonly called warheads.
One component binds to the targeted protein, while the other recruits the cellular machinery responsible for protein degradation.
The reversible linker enables the components to exist as smaller molecules that can more readily penetrate biological membranes.
The molecules are subsequently designed to self-assemble into a functional bifunctional degrader capable of triggering the removal of the intended protein.
Oyster believes this approach could improve central nervous system penetration while preserving the versatility of conventional targeted protein degradation technology.

articles.text:
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:27 AM
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
Eli Radiopharma has raised nearly $60 million (RMB 400 million) in Series A financing to advance its radiopharmaceutical pipeline toward clinical development. The funding will support preclinical research, regulatory submissions, early-stage clinical studies, and the expansion of the company’s research and development capabilities.
Huagai Capital led the financing round, with Bayland Capital serving as co-lead investor. Additional participants included Boyu Ventures, Delian Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Haibang Venture, Bairui Capital, Shenzhen Angel FOF Management, and Grand Flight Investment.
Existing shareholders CSPC & Growth Bio Fund, Huaige Capital, KHK Fund, Longfeng Venture, Hongsheng Capital, Bioclub Fund, and Skyfield Capital also participated in the financing.
Eli Radiopharma plans to allocate the proceeds toward preclinical research, investigational new drug applications, and early-stage clinical development. The company will also strengthen its research platforms, recruit additional talent, expand clinical operations, and pursue business development opportunities.
Founded in 2024, Eli Radiopharma focuses on developing radiopharmaceutical products that combine molecular targeting with radionuclide technology. Its pipeline includes diagnostic and therapeutic candidates designed to address unmet medical needs in oncology and neurological diseases.
The company has advanced multiple programs targeting novel molecular mechanisms through lead discovery, laboratory validation, and animal studies. Several candidates are approaching investigational new drug submissions, representing an important transition from early research toward human clinical testing.
Radiopharmaceuticals combine targeting molecules with radioactive isotopes to identify or treat diseased tissue. Therapeutic radioligands are designed to deliver radiation directly to tumors while limiting exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. Related diagnostic imaging agents can help physicians identify appropriate patients, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment responses.
The financing also reflects growing international interest in radiopharmaceutical innovation originating in China. Global pharmaceutical companies have increasingly explored opportunities involving novel molecular targets, therapeutic radionuclides, and expanded clinical applications.
Eli Radiopharma’s investors identified these areas as important drivers of future industry growth, particularly as radiopharmaceutical technologies move into additional cancer indications and other therapeutic applications.
The company’s longer-term strategy includes building a globally competitive pipeline capable of serving patients in international markets, including the U.S. and Europe. Its immediate priorities involve completing preclinical development, meeting regulatory requirements, and advancing differentiated candidates into clinical studies.
The Series A financing provides Eli Radiopharma with additional resources to move its lead programs closer to clinical validation while expanding the infrastructure needed to support a broader radiopharmaceutical development portfolio.

Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital co-lead $30 million expansion to scale Kindo's go-to-market operations and accelerate development of its AI agent management platform
LOS ANGELES , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kindo , the run-anywhere AI agent management platform that puts the enterprise in control, today announced a $30 million raise co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing total capital raised to $57.6 million. The company grew revenue by approximately 800% year over year in 2026 and will use the financing to expand its go-to-market organization and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.
Continue Reading
Meet Kindo video
As autonomous agents spread through the enterprise and their numbers swell into the thousands, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams struggle to control risks and costs without a centralized tool that can discover, observe, and control the entire enterprise AI footprint. Every time a company lets an AI agent access data, update a customer record, approve a request, or change a production system, it delegates authority. The same permissions that let an agent get work done can let it expose sensitive data, make changes outside company policy, disrupt a critical workflow, or rack up huge inference costs.
"Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business," said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo. "What's missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour. That gap is why the teams responsible for supporting and controlling Al are rightfully putting the brakes on Al transformation."
Kindo gives organizations control of the AI agents already running across their operations. It starts with discovery, uncovering shadow AI and mapping where agents are in use, then brings their activity, access, costs, and outcomes into one view. The teams that must support and control AI, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance, get a single set of controls: what employees can do with an agent, what an agent can touch, how it behaves around the clock, and what it costs. The result is an AI Operations Center, SOC- and NOC-style monitoring and intervention for AI, where those teams eliminate risk, drive down cost, and make sure AI delivers measurable outcomes.
Implementation is turnkey and is run by the IT operations staff an organization already has. Teams connect the agents, data sources, and AI models already in use, and from that moment everything is discovered, observed, and controlled from one place. Kindo's gateways govern and audit every call an agent makes to connected data, tools, and approved models. Identity controls apply the organization's existing permissions to people and agents alike, with the option to tighten them centrally. For mission-critical agents that need deeper control, Kindo's harness, purpose-built for centralized agent operations, adds around-the-clock monitoring, support, and direct intervention, including the ability to take over an agent when something goes wrong.

Key Points LanceDB raised $57.5 million to expand a lakehouse that curates and serves AI training…

LanceDB raised $57.5 million to expand a lakehouse that curates and serves AI training data.
The company reports more than tenfold year-over-year revenue growth since its Series A in June 2025.
LanceDB aims to unify training data, experiments and rollouts so teams stop hand-managing pipelines.
LanceDB announced on November 17, 2026 that it raised $57.5 million in Series B funding to expand its multimodal lakehouse, a platform for organizing and delivering AI training data. The round brings the company’s total funding to $98.5 million.
Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the round, with participation from Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator. LanceDB plans to put the capital toward a broader role across model development, including training-data management, feature engineering, experiment execution and data loading.
Adoption and Technical Scale
LanceDB says researchers can lose weeks or months obtaining and curating training data even though frontier AI advances are measured in days and weeks. Its multimodal lakehouse is intended to close that gap by combining curation, search and retrieval, feature engineering and training for work on frontier models, world models, physical AI and enterprise applications.
The company reports more than tenfold year-over-year revenue growth since its Series A in June 2025. Its open-source library has been downloaded more than 120 million times, representing sixfold growth in total downloads from the same point a year earlier. Customers include Netflix, Microsoft AI, Runway , Luma AI and Midjourney.
The platform is designed to hold multimodal data such as videos, images and sensor data while supporting large-scale retrieval and training. LanceDB says the platform supports more than 130,000 requests per second with latency below 210 milliseconds for 95% of requests, individual tables containing hundreds of petabytes of data or more than 40 billion vectors, and training across 8,000 GPUs in parallel.
Enterprise additions address updates to those tables while they are in use. A durable, memory-accelerated write path handles real-time ingest, distributed indexing scales across large datasets, and managed compaction continuously optimizes tables in the background. LanceDB says managed compaction supports up to 100 billion multimodal rows while multiple researchers concurrently read, write and query the same table.
Customers Describe Changing Training Datasets
Runway CTO Kamil Sindi described how one training example evolves: “A training example at Runway doesn’t stay still. It starts as a video and a prompt, then we add embeddings, resolution and duration metadata, whatever the next experiment needs.” Runway began using the Lance data format in 2024 and later became a LanceDB Enterprise customer. The company now uses Lance and LanceDB Enterprise together so researchers can work through large, changing datasets more quickly.
